title: Finite coefficient-stage data and exactness descent
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and a scheme $W$, with its actual finite coefficient stages and common-stage category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Finite-data representability means that for any finite list of objects and arrows with specified source and target indices, finite list of distinguished triangles [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and finite list of pairs of stage arrows whose images in the common-stage category are equal, one finite stage contains representatives of all these data. Objects have specified inclusion isomorphisms, arrows commute with them, triangles are distinguished and inclusion-isomorphic to the specified triangles, and all the specified equality witnesses become equal at that same stage. Empty lists are allowed. For a morphism $F$ of the actual stage systems of $W$ and another scheme $Z$, t-exact descent is the implication from preservation of both standard halves in all degrees at every finite stage to preservation of both common-stage standard halves. Heart-exact descent is the implication from that same stagewise hypothesis to existence of an additive functor on the common-stage hearts whose included objects and arrows are precisely those of the descended $F$, and which carries every short exact complex to a short exact complex. All standard halves and hearts are the recorded ones [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure].
